newsitem.title: CANADA: Tee-Comm U.S. arm seeks Chapter 11.
newsitem.headline: Tee-Comm U.S. arm seeks Chapter 11.

text.p: Embattled Tee-Comm Electronics Inc. said its U.S. Alphastar satellite provider unit sought Chapter 11 protection after the parent filed for court protection.
Tee-Comm, which entered the U.S. markets too late to compete against the huge U.S. direct-to-home satellite players, also said the Toronto Stock Exchange stopped trading its shares and debentures.
However, Milton, Ontario-based Tee-Comm added its Canadian and U.S. television subscribers still are receiving services.
The Stamford, Conn.-based U.S. service posted liabilities of about US$105 million and assets of about US$72 million in court papers in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court of Delaware.
Tee-Comm also said its president and chief executive Al Bahnman resigned and U.S. arm president David Charles has also left.
Tee-Comm said last week that the Bank of Montreal, its existing lender, demanded immediate repayment of its credit facility and appointed an interim receiver with respect to its property and assets.

Tee-Comm, which had common shares and 9-1/2 percent subordinated convertible debentures traded on the Toronto Stock Exchange, had been competing with GM Hughes Electronics Corp and MCI Communications Corp.
New York's Nasdaq market halted the stock last Thursday after demanding information and justification for continued trading from the company.
